extracted.intended_audience: professional mathematicians and advanced students in geometry and algebra (readers/contributors of 19th-century mathematical journals)
extracted.subtask_description: A 19th‑century mathematical article treating projected circles on the sphere, equal tangents to conics, properties of inscribed polygons, and an extended development of the theory and calculus of symmetric functions — presenting propositions, proofs, methods and corrections. The material is theoretical exposition and proof work in classical analytic and synthetic geometry and algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain and examine every factor in an investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: “the necessity of retaining and of subsequently examining, every factor that may enter into an investigation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not suppress multiplicative factors (such as a or β) in preliminary reductions; retaining them may be essential to determine important properties (e.g., loci). Omitting such factors can prevent identifying indeterminate or special cases. Examine the role of parameters throughout the derivation so all possible cases are evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and indicate every case that can possibly arise
rubrics_metrics.description: “On the other hand, every case that can possibly arise is indicated, both in reference to the parameters of the curves and the position of the point from which the equal tangents are to be drawn.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing a configuration, explicitly enumerate and treat all distinct geometric/algebraic cases (including axis positions, points on the curve, parameter sign/periodicity, coalescing roots). Make loci and special-case loci explicit rather than assuming generic position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check limiting and special configurations
rubrics_metrics.description: E.g., “the curves will have the same form at the limit, when they pass through the pole; therefore all circles which pass through the pole are represented by the equations before given...”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying families of curves or surfaces, evaluate limiting behaviour (e.g., as a parameter → a pole or infinity) and confirm that limiting forms match anticipated special cases (symmetry, degeneracy, asymptotes). Use limits to validate general formulas and identify asymptotes/branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use coordinate/analytical geometry as a primary research instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: “The preceding investigation whilst it exhibits the very comprehensive character of analytical or coordinate geometry as an instrument of research...”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ analytic (coordinate) methods for systematic treatment: reduce geometric problems to algebraic equations, exploit parameterizations, and use algebraic manipulation to derive loci, lengths, curvatures and evolutes. Complement synthetic reasoning with coordinate computations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: When transforming equations choose substitutions that free coefficients from unwanted parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: E.g., in the symmetric-functions discussion: choose transformations so that the coefficients of the transformed equation are free from P (the unwanted parameter); achieve this by suitable choice of substitution constants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select substitutions (such as y = P + Qx + R x^2 + ...) so that target coefficients become independent of specific parameters. The method: impose conditions (critical equations) that determine substitution constants (Q, P, etc.) so the transformed equation's coefficients satisfy desired constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solve the critical equation first when effecting coefficient constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: “In all these cases the critical equation is to be first solved, and the value of Q, so deduced, to be substituted in the second equation. No other kind of elimination is necessary.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-step transformations imposing coefficient conditions (C1 = c1, C2 = c2, ...), first solve the critical (typically nonlinear) equation determining one substitution constant, then substitute that value to solve the remaining (usually simpler) equations. This orders elimination to reduce complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require vanishing of coefficient combinations independently
rubrics_metrics.description: E.g., to make a symmetric-function expression vanish independently of relations among the underlying quantities, force its coefficient combinations (a, b, c) to vanish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When desirous that an expression vanish identically (for arbitrary underlying variables), enforce that each independent coefficient or combination of coefficients is zero. Translate this into algebraic conditions on parameters and solve them explicitly (e.g., choose X' = -1 to satisfy three simultaneous relations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt general theorems to configuration constraints (check hypotheses carefully)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of applying Desargues' theorem: when the line neither cuts nor touches the conic section, the theorem 'requires modification to adapt it to this demonstration.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before applying a classical theorem (Desargues, involution, etc.), verify that its hypotheses hold in the present configuration; if not, adapt the theorem (e.g., introduce auxiliary points or a subsidiary conic) and show the modified statements cover the exceptional geometric positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proportional division and parallel-plane arguments in synthetic proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple propositions show use of parallel planes and proportional division (e.g., 'If three straight lines be parallel to one plane ... then all straight lines resting upon them will be divided proportionally').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For spatial geometry and twisted quadrilaterals/ruled surfaces, structure proofs via constructing parallel planes, drawing parallels through points, and deriving proportional relationships between segment divisions. Exploit similarity of triangles and parallelograms to obtain proportionalities and concurrency/intersection results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish and apply corrections/errata for earlier formulae
rubrics_metrics.description: The author notes explicit corrections (e.g., 'The reader will be pleased to make the following corrections...') and corrects coefficients used in earlier volume pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When prior published formulae are found in error, provide explicit line-by-line corrections and indicate their propagation into later derivations. Recompute affected derived expressions (e.g., critical functions) and state the corrected simplified forms to maintain reproducibility.
